rows.q: What is the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen for adults?
rows.answer: The maximum daily dose of acetaminophen for adults is 4,000 mg per day [1]. This includes all routes of administration and all acetaminophen-containing products, including combination products [1].

rows.q: Can I take ibuprofen during the third trimester of pregnancy?
rows.answer:
According to the sources, ibuprofen should be avoided during the third trimester of pregnancy because it may cause premature closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus [1][2][6].

Not covered by the sources: The sources do not provide information on the specific risks or effects of taking ibuprofen during the third trimester beyond the risk of premature closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus.

rows.q: What is the boxed warning for warfarin?
rows.answer:
The boxed warning for warfarin is:

WARNING: BLEEDING RISK • Warfarin sodium can cause major or fatal bleeding [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1) ] . • Perform regular monitoring of INR in all treated patients [see Dosage and Administration (2.1) ] . • Drugs, dietary changes, and other factors affect INR levels achieved with warfarin sodium therapy [see Drug Interactions (7) ] . • Instruct patients about prevention measures to minimize risk of bleeding and to report signs and symptoms of bleeding [see Patient Counseling Information (17) ] .

[1]

The boxed warning also states that warfarin sodium can cause major or fatal bleeding. [1]

The following serious adverse reactions to warfarin sodium are discussed in greater detail in other sections of the labeling: • Hemorrhage [see Boxed Warning , Warnings and Precautions (5.1) , and Overdosage (10) ] [2]

Most common adverse reactions to warfarin sodium are fatal and nonfatal hemorrhage from any tissue or organ. [2]

rows.q: How should lisinopril be dosed for hypertension in adults?
rows.answer: The recommended initial dose of lisinopril for hypertension in adults is 10 mg once a day [1]. Dosage should be adjusted according to blood pressure response [1]. The usual dosage range is 20 mg to 40 mg per day administered in a single daily dose [1]. Doses up to 80 mg have been used but do not appear to give greater effect [1]. The initial dose in adult patients with hypertension taking diuretics is 5 mg once per day [1].

rows.q: What are the common side effects of atorvastatin?
rows.answer:
The most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5%) are nasopharyngitis, arthralgia, diarrhea, pain in extremity, and urinary tract infection [1]. 

Common adverse reactions that led to treatment discontinuation and occurred at a rate greater than placebo were: myalgia (0.7%), diarrhea (0.5%), nausea (0.4%), alanine aminotransferase increase (0.4%), and hepatic enzyme increase (0.4%) [3].

rows.q: Is sertraline safe for children?
rows.answer:
The safety and effectiveness of sertraline hydrochloride in pediatric patients other than those with OCD have not been established [1][4]. Safety and effectiveness in pediatric patients in patients with OCD below the age of 6 have not been established [3]. Two placebo-controlled trials were conducted in pediatric patients with MDD, but the data were not sufficient to support an indication for use in pediatric patients [3].

However, the safety and efficacy of sertraline hydrochloride have been established in the treatment of OCD in pediatric patients aged 6 to 17 [3]. Monitoring Pediatric Patients Treated with Sertraline Hydrochloride: Monitor all patients being treated with antidepressants for clinical worsening, suicidal thoughts, and unusual changes in behavior, especially during the initial few months of treatment, or at times of dose increases or decreases [3].

Decreased appetite and weight loss have been observed with the use of SSRIs [3]. Monitor weight and growth in pediatric patients treated with an SSRI such as sertraline hydrochloride [3].

rows.q: What should I avoid while taking metronidazole?
rows.answer: Avoid consuming alcoholic beverages or products containing propylene glycol while taking metronidazole and for at least three days afterward [2]. This is because abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, headaches, and flushing may occur [2]. Do not administer metronidazole to patients who have taken disulfiram within the last two weeks [3]. Metronidazole has been reported to potentiate the anticoagulant effect of warfarin and other oral coumarin anticoagulants, resulting in a prolongation of prothrombin time [3]. Monitor prothrombin time and INR when metronidazole is prescribed for patients on this type of anticoagulant therapy [3].

rows.q: How do I take levothyroxine with food?
rows.answer: Administer Levothyroxine Sodium Tablets on an empty stomach, one-half to one hour before breakfast [1]. Do not take Levothyroxine Sodium Tablets within 4 hours of certain foods that may affect absorption, such as soybean-based infant formula [1]. Do not store the suspension of Levothyroxine Sodium Tablets in foods that decrease absorption, such as soybean-based infant formula [1]. Administer Levothyroxine Sodium Tablets as a single daily dose, preferably on an empty stomach, one-half to one hour before breakfast [2]. Do not take Levothyroxine Sodium Tablets within 4 hours of agents such as iron and calcium supplements and antacids, which can decrease the absorption of levothyroxine [4].

rows.q: What is the starting dose of gabapentin for postherpetic neuralgia?
rows.answer: The starting dose of gabapentin for postherpetic neuralgia is a single 300 mg dose on Day 1 [1]. The dose can be titrated up to 600 mg/day on Day 2 [1]. The dose can be further titrated up to 900 mg/day on Day 3 [1].

rows.q: Does amoxicillin interact with oral contraceptives?
rows.answer: Amoxicillin may affect the intestinal flora, leading to lower estrogen reabsorption and reduced efficacy of combined oral estrogen/progesterone contraceptives [1]. Amoxicillin may reduce the efficacy of oral contraceptives [2].

rows.q: What is the dose of omeprazole for GERD?
rows.answer:
For symptomatic GERD, the dose of omeprazole is:
* 5 mg once daily for up to 4 weeks for patients 5 to less than 10 kg [1]
* 10 mg once daily for up to 4 weeks for patients 10 to less than 20 kg [1]
* 20 mg once daily for up to 4 weeks for patients 20 kg and greater [1]

For EE due to Acid-Mediated GERD, the dose of omeprazole is:
* 5 mg once daily for 4 to 8 weeks for patients 5 to less than 10 kg [2]
* 10 mg once daily for 4 to 8 weeks for patients 10 to less than 20 kg [2]
* 20 mg once daily for 4 to 8 weeks for patients 20 kg and greater [2]

Note: The efficacy of omeprazole used for longer than 8 weeks in patients with EE has not been established [5].

rows.q: What are the contraindications of sildenafil?
rows.answer: Sildenafil tablets are contraindicated in patients with a known hypersensitivity to sildenafil, as contained in sildenafil tablets and REVATIO, or any component of the tablet [1]. Hypersensitivity reactions have been reported, including rash and urticaria [1]. Administration of sildenafil tablets to patients using nitric oxide donors, such as organic nitrates or organic nitrites in any form, is contraindicated [2]. Sildenafil tablets were shown to potentiate the hypotensive effect of nitrates [2]. Known hypersensitivity to sildenafil or any component of tablet is a contraindication [2]. Administration with guanylate cyclase (GC) stimulators, such as riociguat, is contraindicated [2]. Nitrates are contraindicated with sildenafil tablets [3]. Consistent with its known effects on the nitric oxide/cGMP pathway, sildenafil tablets were shown to potentiate the hypotensive effects of nitrates [3]. After patients have taken sildenafil tablets, it is unknown when nitrates, if necessary, can be safely administered [3]. Do not use sildenafil tablets in patients who are using a GC stimulator, such as riociguat [4]. PDE5 inhibitors, including sildenafil tablets, may potentiate the hypotensive effects of GC stimulators [4].
